Bellerophon. A warrior of noble birth, grandson of Sisyphus, who became the hero most renowned for slaying the Chimera. His early life was marked by exile and false accusations, burdens he carried with him into his heroic deeds.

His greatest achievement was made possible by an extraordinary discovery. Bellerophon tamed Pegasus, the divine winged horse that had been born from the blood of Medusa after her death. Few mortals could have captured and controlled such a creature, but Bellerophon managed the feat and found in Pegasus an ally unlike any other.

With Pegasus beneath him, Bellerophon confronted the Chimera, a fire-breathing hybrid monster that was perhaps the most terrifying of all creatures. It had the head of a lion, the body of a goat, and the tail of a serpent, and its breath was flame that could consume entire armies. Bellerophon rode Pegasus above the monster and struck it down with his spear from the air, attacking from a height where the Chimera could not reach him. The victory established his lasting fame.

His success led to more seemingly impossible tasks. A jealous king set him to fight the fierce Amazons, the warrior women of legend, and to complete other dangerous challenges. Each time, Bellerophon succeeded. Each victory added to his renown and his pride in his own accomplishments. But his pride became his undoing.

Emboldened by his achievements, Bellerophon grew convinced that his own excellence had elevated him above other men, and he resolved to attempt something no mortal should consider. He tried to ride Pegasus to Mount Olympus itself, to join the gods as an equal. But Zeus would not tolerate such arrogance. The king of the gods struck, and Bellerophon was thrown from Pegasus. He fell from the heavens to earth below, stripped by divine punishment of his strength and his sight. He lived out his remaining days blind and lame, a hero broken by hubris, remembered as much for his fall as for his triumphs.
